newsitem.title: GERMANY: Zeitler upbeat on prices but urges vigilance.
newsitem.headline: Zeitler upbeat on prices but urges vigilance.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler said on Wednesday he remained optimistic on the outlook for German prices but added that recent inflation data gave cause to be vigilant.

Speaking to reporters in Bonn, Zeitler also said Germany still had a "realistic" prospect of meeting the Maastricht Treaty's deficit requirement for countries seeking to qualify for European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
The Treaty says a country's budget deficit must not exceed three percent of gross domestic product (GDP), but it does allow for exceptions.
Zeitler said the national government, federal states and municipalities would have to make a joint effort to consolidate their budgets.
Zeitler also said he saw no upward pressure on import prices at the moment.
He added that Germany's proposed tax reform would benefit the economy, provided that it was implemented in full.
